purpose: Fix the acceptance bars for ASSISTS and CARDS before either is modelled. Committed alone, as with every model measured on this repository.

targets.definition: did this player register one or more assists
did this player receive one or more cards, yellow or red

whyTheseLines: Over 0.5 for both, from DESIGN DATA ONLY (2022-23 + 2023-24 appearances). Any longer line is empty: assists over 1.5 occurs 0.48% of the time and cards over 1.5 0.19%, because a second yellow IS a red and the player leaves the pitch. Base rates at the chosen line are 6.75% for assists and 13.44% for cards.
independence: Judged SEPARATELY against identical bars, both verdicts recorded whichever way they fall — as with shots, where one target passed and the other did not.
expectationsStatedUPFRONT: Both of these are expected to be HARDER than shots on goal, and saying so before the run matters more than saying it after. Assists depend on what a teammate does with the pass and are notoriously low-repeatability at the player level. Cards depend heavily on the referee and the state of the match, and this model has neither: no referee assignment, no scoreline, no match context. In both cases the POSITIONAL baseline is already strong — assists run 0.39% for keepers against 12.63% for forwards, and cards 6.83% for substitutes against 18.28% for midfielders — so there may be little room left for player-specific history to add anything. A rejection here would be an ordinary outcome, not a surprise.

population.rule: every player who APPEARED — started or came off the bench
population.honestLimitation: Conditions on participation; does not predict whether a player will play.

protocol.walkForward: by match date; rates fitted STRICTLY on earlier-dated matches

warmup.rule: folds into the rates, NEVER scored

development.use: ALL hyperparameter search happens here and nowhere else

holdout.use: scored ONCE, after the configuration is locked

protocol.holdoutDisclosure: 2025-26 has now been scored twice — once under the voided goalscorer v1 run, and once for shots and shots on goal. Those were DIFFERENT targets; no assists or cards hyperparameter has ever touched it and no assist or card outcome from it has been observed. This is the third look at that season for a third pair of targets, and it is disclosed rather than glossed so the reader can weigh it. It is also the last: after this, a new target needs a new season, not another pass over the same one.

model.form: a shrunk per-appearance rate for the player's participation state, converted to P(count > line)
model.shrinkage: Bayesian pseudo-count k toward the positional rate for the same state
model.distributionNote: Poisson and negative binomial are both in the grid for consistency with the shots protocol, with one recorded consequence: CARDS ARE UNDERDISPERSED in the design data (variance/mean 0.89, where Poisson requires 1.0), so the negative binomial has no positive method-of-moments solution and the implementation falls back to Poisson. The two grid arms therefore coincide for cards. That is stated rather than hidden, and it is the correct behaviour — an underdispersed count has no negative-binomial fit to find.

baselines.definition: the league base rate for (position group x participation state), fitted on prior matches only
the player's unshrunk historical rate, positional as fallback

primaryMetric: log loss on the binary over/under outcome
secondaryMetrics: predicted vs observed count clearing the line

acceptanceBars.note: IDENTICAL to the goalscorer and shots bars. Not softened because these markets are expected to be harder — that is exactly when a bar is doing its job.

bars.statement: model HOLDOUT log loss must be lower than the positional baseline's by at least 0.005
model HOLDOUT log loss must be lower than or equal to the raw-player baseline's
model HOLDOUT expected calibration error must be at most 0.020
summed predicted probabilities must land within 10% of the observed number clearing the line
the model must produce a probability for at least 95% of the appeared population

stoppingRule.statement: ONE sweep over the declared grid per target, on DEVELOPMENT only. A target clearing all five bars publishes; a target that does not is REJECTED, stays unpublished, and is not re-specified on this corpus.

whatPassingDoesNotMean: It does not mean the model beats a sportsbook price. No player-prop odds are ingested.
For cards specifically, it would not mean the model understands refereeing — it has no referee input at all.
It does not answer whether a player will play.
